chunks: And from him (the previous narrator) it was said: Wahb narrated to them from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a woman who had a child from another man, and the child died leaving property, he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is appropriate for the husband to separate from the wife until she menstruates once, to purify her womb; I fear that a pregnancy might occur in her, so the heir would be one who has no right to inheritance.'
Abu Ali said: And this is also contrary to the truth and is not taken; rather, the inheritance belongs to the mother of the deceased.

key_terms.يَسْتَبْرِئُ رَحِمَهَا: to purify/verify the womb (ensure no pregnancy)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for a stepchild who dies leaving property, and what is the role of the stepfather?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the legal precaution (*istibra'*) a stepfather must observe to distinguish his potential offspring from the deceased husband's child, ensuring accurate inheritance distribution. Abu Ali highlights a scholarly nuance, noting that while the Imam emphasizes preventing paternity confusion, the ultimate inheritance right firmly belongs to the mother, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maternal lineage in the absence of other heirs. This ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic inheritance laws within the context of blended families and uncertain paternity.
